letters.name: a
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'a' in English 'about' — short, neutral, and relaxed. This is Hindi's inherent vowel, the one hiding inside every consonant.

letters.name: ā
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'a' in English 'father' — hold it longer than the short अ. Think of the doctor saying 'say aah.'

letters.name: i
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'i' in English 'sit' — short, crisp, and front-of-mouth. Do NOT say it like 'eye'.

letters.name: ī
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ee' in English 'see' — smile wide and let the sound stretch twice as long as इ. Think of a happy 'eeee!'

letters.name: u
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'u' in English 'put' — short, with lips slightly rounded but relaxed. Think of saying 'uh-oh' without the 'oh.'

letters.name: ū
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'oo' in English 'food' — purse your lips tightly and hold it long. Imagine a ghost going 'oooo.'

letters.name: ṛ
letters.memoryTrick: A rolled 'r' followed by short 'i' — like 'ri' in 'river' but with a quick tongue tap. In modern Hindi often pronounced like 'ri' in 'rich.'

letters.name: e
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ay' in English 'say' but a pure, long vowel — no glide at the end. Think of the Canadian 'eh?' held steady.

letters.name: ai
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'a' in English 'cat' but held long — open your mouth wider than for ए. Imagine a doctor pressing your tongue down: 'aaaai.'

letters.name: o
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'o' in English 'go' but clipped — no rounding-off at the end. Pure, steady, and round like your lips making an 'O.'

letters.name: au
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'aw' in English 'saw' — deep and open. Think of the sound you make when you see something cute: 'aww.'

letters.name: ka
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'k' in English 'skate' — crisp and unaspirated. Hold a tissue in front of your mouth; it should NOT move when you say it.

letters.name: kha
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'k' with a strong puff of air — similar to 'ck-h' in 'black hat' said fast. That tissue should flutter.

letters.name: ga
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'g' in English 'go' — voiced but without the puff of air. Your vocal cords should vibrate.

letters.name: gha
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'g' but with a breathy, murmured release — imagine saying 'g' while sighing. A deep, throaty voiced puff.

letters.name: ṅa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ng' in English 'sing' — the sound at the back of your throat. This letter almost never starts a Hindi word; it appears inside words before क, ख, ग, घ.

letters.name: ca
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ch' in English 'church' but softer — unaspirated. Your tongue touches the roof of your mouth lightly.

letters.name: cha
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ch' with a strong puff of air — imagine sneezing while saying 'church.' The aspirated version of च.

letters.name: ja
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'j' in English 'jug' — voiced and soft, no puff. Your tongue presses against the roof of your mouth just behind your teeth.

letters.name: jha
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'j' with a breathy release — imagine saying 'jug' while sighing heavily. A murmured, voiced 'jh' sound.

letters.name: ña
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'ny' in English 'canyon' or Spanish 'mañana' — the tongue touches the hard palate. Very rare at the start of words.

letters.name: ṭa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 't' but curl your tongue way back to touch the roof of your mouth — a hard, retroflex sound. Like the 't' in an Indian-accented 'top.'

letters.name: ṭha
letters.memoryTrick: Like ठ is to ट what ख is to क — same retroflex tongue position but with a strong puff of air. Imagine a forceful 'th' with tongue curled back.

letters.name: ḍa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'd' but with your tongue curled back retroflex — deeper and harder than regular English 'd.' Your tongue taps the roof further back.

letters.name: ḍha
letters.memoryTrick: Like ड with a heavy, breathy release — curl your tongue back for the retroflex 'd' then sigh through it. A deep, throaty voiced puff.

letters.name: ṇa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'n' but with your tongue curled back retroflex — deeper than English 'n.' The 'n' in many Indian-accented English words. Almost never starts a Hindi word.

letters.name: ta
letters.memoryTrick: Like 't' but with your tongue touching your teeth (dental), not the roof of your mouth. Think of the French or Spanish 't' — softer and more forward.

letters.name: tha
letters.memoryTrick: Like 't' with teeth-touching position plus a puff of air — imagine saying 'table' while breathing out hard. Dental and aspirated.

letters.name: da
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'th' in English 'this' — a soft, dental 'd' with tongue touching the back of your top teeth. Not the hard English 'd.'

letters.name: dha
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'd' with your tongue on your teeth plus a breathy release — imagine saying 'the' while exhaling warmly. Voiced dental with a sigh.

letters.name: na
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'n' in English 'name' — tongue touches your teeth (dental), just like त and द. It's the regular, everyday Hindi 'n.'

letters.name: pa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'p' in English 'spot' — crisp, unaspirated, with lips pressed together. No puff of air; the tissue stays still.

letters.name: pha
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'p' with a strong puff of air — say 'pin' but really breathe out. The tissue test: it should flutter noticeably.

letters.name: ba
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'b' in English 'boy' — lips together, voiced, no puff. Your vocal cords vibrate as you open your lips.

letters.name: bha
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'b' with a breathy, murmured release — imagine saying 'boy' while sighing heavily through your nose. Voiced and aspirated.

letters.name: ma
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'm' in English 'mother' — lips together, hum through your nose. Same warm, nasal sound in every language.

letters.name: ya
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'y' in English 'yes' — a smooth, palatal glide. Your tongue approaches the roof of your mouth without fully touching.

letters.name: ra
letters.memoryTrick: A quick tongue-tap 'r' like the Spanish single 'r' in 'pero' or the 'dd' in American English 'ladder.' Not the rolled Scottish 'r.'

letters.name: la
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'l' in English 'love' — tongue touches the back of your top teeth. A clear, bright 'l,' never the dark 'l' of English 'full.'

letters.name: va
letters.memoryTrick: Between English 'v' and 'w' — lips approach each other but don't quite touch. Like a very soft 'v' or a slightly buzzy 'w.'

letters.name: śa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'sh' in English 'shoe' — tongue near the roof of your mouth, palatal. The most common Hindi 'sh' sound.

letters.name: ṣa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'sh' but with your tongue curled back (retroflex) — deeper and harder than श. Imagine saying 'sh' while pulling your tongue back.

letters.name: sa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 's' in English 'sun' — a clean, dental hiss with tongue near your teeth. The everyday Hindi 's' you'll use most often.

letters.name: ha
letters.memoryTrick: A voiced, breathy 'h' — like the 'h' in English 'behind' or the sound of a gentle sigh. Your vocal cords vibrate while air passes through.

letters.name: kṣa
letters.memoryTrick: A conjunct of क + ष — sounds like 'ksh' as in 'backshift.' Start with a crisp 'k' and slide into a retroflex 'sh.'

letters.name: tra
letters.memoryTrick: A conjunct of त + र — like 'tr' in English 'tree' but with a dental 't' (tongue on teeth). Quick transition from 't' to rolled 'r.'

letters.name: jña
letters.memoryTrick: A conjunct of ज + ञ — in modern Hindi pronounced like 'gya' as in 'gyat.' Imagine saying 'g' and 'y' together quickly. Some regions say 'dnya.'

letters.name: qa
letters.memoryTrick: Like a 'k' made deep in the throat, way back near your uvula — imagine the Arabic 'Qaf.' Borrowed from Persian/Arabic for words like 'qalam' (pen). The dot underneath क signals this deeper sound.

letters.name: xa
letters.memoryTrick: Like the 'ch' in Scottish 'loch' or German 'Bach' — a throaty, fricative sound like clearing your throat gently. The dot under ख turns the aspirated 'kh' into this guttural sound.

letters.name: ġa
letters.memoryTrick: Like the French 'r' in 'Paris' or a voiced version of ख़ — a soft, gargling sound made with vibrating vocal cords. Rare in everyday Hindi.

letters.name: za
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'z' in English 'zebra' — a voiced buzzing 's.' The dot under ज turns the 'j' sound into this familiar 'z.' Very common in Hindi.

letters.name: ṛa
letters.memoryTrick: A retroflex flap — like the 'rd' in an American 'ladder' said quickly, but with your tongue curled back. A single tap of the curled tongue. Never starts a word.

letters.name: ṛha
letters.memoryTrick: Like ड़ but with a breathy release — the retroflex flap followed by a puff of air. The aspirated version of the flap. Appears in very few Hindi words.

letters.name: fa
letters.memoryTrick: Like 'f' in English 'fun' — top teeth on bottom lip, blow air through. The dot under फ turns the aspirated 'ph' into the familiar 'f.' Very common in modern Hindi.

letters.name: ā mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: The vertical line after a consonant lengthens the inherent 'a' to 'ā' — like क becomes का (kā). Think of it as stretching the short 'a' sound.

letters.name: i mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: The curved stroke before a consonant adds a short 'i' — like क becomes कि (ki). It sits to the LEFT of the consonant even though the 'i' sound comes AFTER it.

letters.name: ī mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: The curved stroke after a consonant gives a long 'ī' — like क becomes की (kī). It looks like a mirror-image of the short ि matra, now sitting on the right.

letters.name: u mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: The small hook underneath a consonant adds a short 'u' — like क becomes कु (ku). It's a tiny curve that hangs below the letter.

letters.name: ū mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: The curl underneath a consonant gives a long 'ū' — like क becomes कू (kū). It's the extended version of the short u hook, curving further.

letters.name: ṛ mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: The half-moon underneath a consonant adds 'ṛ' — like क becomes कृ (kṛ). Looks like a tiny crescent hanging below the letter. Rare in everyday words.

letters.name: e mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: The slanted stroke above a consonant gives 'e' — like क becomes के (ke). It sits on top, like a little roof over the letter.

letters.name: ai mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: Two slanted strokes above a consonant give 'ai' — like क becomes कै (kai). It's like the e mātrā with an extra stroke, opening the sound wider.

letters.name: o mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: The e mātrā े plus the ā mātrā ा after the consonant gives 'o' — like क becomes को (ko). It's a two-part diacritic that wraps around the letter.

letters.name: au mātrā
letters.memoryTrick: The ai mātrā ै plus the ā mātrā ा after the consonant gives 'au' — like क becomes कौ (kau). The two-part wrapper that opens into a deep 'aw' sound.

letters.name: anusvāra
letters.memoryTrick: The dot above a letter adds a nasal sound — like in रंग (raṅg, color). It's like the 'n' in French 'bon' or the nasal hum at the end of 'sing.'

letters.name: candrabindu
letters.memoryTrick: The crescent with a dot (moon-dot) above a vowel nasalizes it — like in हाँ (hā̃, yes). Think of it as the 'n' sound creeping into the vowel. 'Chandra' means moon.

letters.name: visarga
letters.memoryTrick: Two dots after a letter add a breathy 'h' echo — like a whispered puff after the vowel. Rare in everyday Hindi, mostly in Sanskrit loanwords like दुःख (duḥkh, sorrow).

letters.name: virāma / halant
letters.memoryTrick: The small diagonal stroke underneath a consonant removes its inherent 'a' vowel — like क् (k instead of ka). It's the 'silencer' that lets consonants stack into conjuncts like क्त (kt).
